dataset_info.disclosure: HAND-AUTHORED SYNTHETIC TEST DATA. Every 'message' in this file was written by a human/agent for evaluation purposes. None of it is real customer data, real conversation transcripts, or real leads. Do not treat any message, name, email, or phone number below as belonging to a real person.
dataset_info.author: Task 5.1 (LeadGate eval harness)
dataset_info.source_of_truth_for_labels: data/cars_raw.csv (350 rows) as of the date above; make/model/price facts used to construct genuine no-match cases were verified against this exact file.
known_limitations_reflected_in_labels: CarsAdapter.search_inventory (engine/adapters/cars.py) only applies 'price_max' as an actual Odoo domain filter. The 'make' and 'model' arguments are part of the tool schema and SHOULD be extracted correctly by the LLM (that is what expected_tool/expected_args test), but the adapter does not currently filter on them server-side. This mirrors the already-documented real_estate property_type/bedrooms limitation from Task 2.2's review, just not previously written down for cars. Where this matters for a case's real-world outcome, expected_outcome says so explicitly.
price_max is falsy-checked in the adapter (`if args.get('price_max')`), so a price_max of 0 would be silently ignored. No case in this file uses price_max: 0 deliberately for that reason.
dataset_info.grading_note: expected_tool/expected_args are graded against what a correctly-behaving LLM SHOULD call (tool selection + argument extraction). expected_outcome additionally describes the real downstream result given the adapter's current, known-limited filtering behavior, so Task 5.2's runner can distinguish 'the LLM chose right' from 'the system produced the right answer end-to-end'.

cases.message: Do you have any Mazda CX-5 under $30,000?
cases.expected_outcome: Correct tool call with make/model/price_max extracted. cars_raw.csv has two CX-5 rows (28510, 18615), both under 30000. Since price_max IS actually applied by the adapter, the real result will correctly include only cars <= 30000, but because make/model are not filtered server-side, other makes under 30000 will also appear in the returned matches.

cases.expected_outcome: Ford Mustang rows in cars_raw.csv: 46160, 33440, 16960 -- two of three are under 35000. price_max filtering works; make/model filtering does not (known limitation), so results will include non-Mustangs priced under 35000 too.

cases.message: I want an SUV, but nothing too expensive
cases.expected_outcome: 'SUV' isn't a make/model field and 'not too expensive' has no concrete number. A reasonable LLM either asks a clarifying question about budget or calls search_inventory with a guessed low-to-mid price_max. Exact args not strictly graded.

cases.message: Looking for something fuel efficient
cases.expected_outcome: No make/model/price extractable. search_inventory with empty args acceptable; not strictly graded on args.

cases.message: What do you have in stock right now?
cases.expected_outcome: General browse request maps cleanly to search_inventory with no filters. This is the clearest of the ambiguous cases -- args should genuinely be empty here.

cases.message: Any deals on used trucks?
cases.expected_outcome: 'Used trucks' and 'deals' are not schema fields (condition/status aren't LLM-settable args here). search_inventory with empty args is acceptable; not strictly graded on args.

cases.message: Do you have any Porsche 911s?
cases.expected_outcome: Verified against cars_raw.csv: Porsche does not appear anywhere in the 350-row make list. A correct implementation would return zero matches. NOTE: because the adapter does not actually filter by make (known limitation), the real system will currently return other available cars instead of an honest empty result -- this case is useful for catching that specific regression/limitation, not just LLM tool-call correctness.

cases.message: I'm looking for a Ferrari, any in stock?
cases.expected_outcome: Ferrari is absent from cars_raw.csv's make list. Correct behavior is zero matches; current adapter will not actually enforce that due to the make-filtering limitation described in dataset_info.

cases.expected_outcome: Rivian is absent from cars_raw.csv (the only EVs are Tesla Model 3/Model Y, Chevy Bolt/Blazer EV, Kia EV6, Hyundai Ioniq 5, Nissan Ariya). Correct behavior is zero matches; adapter limitation as above applies.

cases.message: I want an Alfa Romeo Giulia
cases.expected_outcome: Alfa Romeo is absent from cars_raw.csv. Correct behavior is zero matches; adapter limitation as above applies.

cases.message: Do you have a Toyota under $10,000?
cases.expected_outcome: Genuinely no match on TWO independent grounds: the cheapest car in the entire cars_raw.csv is 13890 (a Jeep Grand Cherokee), so nothing at all is under 10000, and separately no Toyota row is anywhere near that price. Because price_max IS actually applied by the adapter, this case is reliable end-to-end -- the real system should correctly return zero matches regardless of the make-filtering limitation.

cases.message: Anything at all under $5,000?
cases.expected_outcome: The cheapest car in cars_raw.csv is 13890. price_max=5000 is genuinely below every seeded price, and since price_max filtering is real (not subject to the make/model limitation), the system should correctly return zero matches end-to-end.

cases.message: Do you have a Ford F150 for under $15,000?
cases.expected_outcome: No Ford F150 row is anywhere near 15000 (the cheapest F150 in cars_raw.csv is 20022) -- a correct, fully-filtering implementation would return zero matches. HOWEVER the overall cheapest cars in cars_raw.csv (Jeep Grand Cherokee 13890, Volkswagen Jetta 14355, Acura MDX 14740, Lincoln MKZ 14865) ARE under 15000, so because the adapter only filters price_max and ignores make, the current system will incorrectly return those non-F150 cars as if they matched. This case is intentionally chosen to expose that exact limitation -- label the 'correct' expected result as zero, but expect the current implementation to fail this case honestly.
